'''Cristina Manolache''' is a mathematician and Senior Lecturer in the School of Mathematics and Statistics at the [[University of Sheffield]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dr Cristina Manolache|url=https://maths.dept.shef.ac.uk/maths/staff_info_910.html|url-status=live|access-date=8 April 2021|website=The University of Sheffield|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191004085938/http://maths.dept.shef.ac.uk:80/maths/staff_info_910.html |archive-date=2019-10-04 }}</ref>

==Education and career==

Manolache received her PhD in Mathematics from [[SISSA]] in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|title=SISSA profile page|url=https://www.math.sissa.it/users/cristina-manolache|access-date=2021-05-12}}</ref> Her dissertation, Virtual Intersections,<ref name=":0" /> was supervised by [[Barbara Fantechi]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite thesis|last=Manolache|first=Cristina|date=2008–2009|title=Virtual Intersections|type=PhD Thesis |url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/287417759.pdf|publisher=Scuola Internazionale Superiore di Studi Avanzati}}</ref> Manolache specializes in [[algebraic geometry]] and has expertise in birational geometry and wall crossings.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Video: Cristina Manolache, "A splitting of the virtual class"|url=http://www.birs.ca/events/2018/5-day-workshops/18w5084/videos/watch/201810091400-Manolache.html?jwsource=cl|access-date=2021-04-09|website=www.birs.ca}}</ref> She has contributed to publications of the [[American Mathematical Society]] and [[Cambridge University Press]]. Notable publications include Reduced invariants from cuspidal maps (2020),<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Battistella|first1=Luca|last2=Carocci|first2=Francesca|last3=Manolache|first3=Cristina|date=2020|title=Reduced invariants from cuspidal maps|url=https://www.ams.org/tran/2020-373-09/S0002-9947-2020-08141-0/|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society|language=en|volume=373|issue=9|pages=6713–6756|doi=10.1090/tran/8141|issn=0002-9947|doi-access=free|arxiv=1801.07739}}</ref> co-authored with Luca Battistella and Francesca Carocci; Stable maps and stable quotients (2014);<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Manolache|first=Cristina|date=2014|title=Stable maps and stable quotients|journal=Compositio Mathematica|language=en|volume=150|issue=9|pages=1457–1481|doi=10.1112/S0010437X14007258|issn=0010-437X|doi-access=free|arxiv=1301.4393}}</ref> Virtual pull-backs] (2012);<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/jag/2012-21-02/S1056-3911-2011-00606-1/home.html|doi = 10.1090/S1056-3911-2011-00606-1|title = Virtual pull-backs|year = 2011|last1 = Manolache|first1 = Cristina|journal = Journal of Algebraic Geometry|volume = 21|issue = 2|pages = 201–245|s2cid = 16201909|doi-access = free}}</ref> and Virtual push-forwards (2012).<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Manolache|first=Cristina|date=2012-08-31|title=Virtual push-forwards|url=https://msp.org/gt/2012/16-4/p03.xhtml|journal=Geometry & Topology|volume=16|issue=4|pages=2003–2036|doi=10.2140/gt.2012.16.2003|issn=1364-0380|doi-access=free|arxiv=1010.2704}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==

Manolache was awarded the [[Emmy Noether Fellowship]] in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=LMS Emmy Noether Fellows 2020 Announced {{!}} London Mathematical Society|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news-entry/09072020-1421/lms-emmy-noether-fellows-2020-announced|access-date=2021-04-08|website=www.lms.ac.uk}}</ref>
